summary: Step 2 of the fork-based browser build: the reader decides between generating a new signing keystore and uploading an existing one, which determines whether AAPS can later be updated in place. It also explains GitHub secrets and how to export the stored keystore to Google Drive with a workflow. Labels are GitHub's.

sections.heading: Browser build – Step 2: Create your signing keystore
sections.summary: Page title; why the keystore choice matters for future updates, and what a GitHub secret is.

sections.heading: Option 1 – Generate a new keystore (new users)
sections.summary: When to generate a new keystore, and the warning that the result cannot update an existing AAPS install without export, uninstall and reimport.

sections.heading: Option 2 – Upload your existing keystore (existing / past users)
sections.summary: When to upload an existing Android Studio keystore, which keeps the current install upgradeable.

sections.heading: Export your keystore (optional)
sections.summary: Introduces exporting the stored keystore as a password-protected ZIP to Google Drive.

sections.heading: Steps:
sections.summary: In the GitHub repository: add a ZIP_PASSWORD secret under Settings, then run the CI KeyStore Export workflow from Actions.
